evals.prompt: Review PR #231 for layering violations. It adds a 'refund' use case to our Kotlin backend (modules: api, application, domain, infrastructure).
evals.expected_output: Runs git diff --stat base...HEAD (or gh pr diff) and reads the full diff; loads intended-architecture sources (ADRs, arch tests, build files) for touched modules; classifies the change; maps each new import edge onto an allowed-dependency table and flags e.g. domain importing an infrastructure/ORM/HTTP type with an OBSERVED file:line and quoted import; checks bypassed ports, idempotency of the refund, timeouts on the payment call, contract changes; returns the PR-variant report with a verdict (Approve / Approve with follow-ups / Request changes), at most ~7 findings each with severity, confidence, threatened QA, evidence, concrete fix, effort S/M/L and a preventing fitness function (e.g. ArchUnit or Konsist rule). No style nits.

evals.prompt: Design a notification service (email, SMS, push) for our platform. It must keep accepting requests when a provider is down and deliver 99% of messages within 10 seconds at 500 msg/s peak. We're a TypeScript/Node shop.
evals.expected_output: Follows the build workflow: brief recon; asks at most 3-5 structure-changing questions or marks ASSUMED; writes 3-7 six-part scenarios with numeric response measures (availability under provider outage, latency p99, throughput) marked CONFIRMED/ASSUMED and a utility tree rated H/M/L; maps tactics (e.g. queue/asynchrony, retry with backoff, circuit breaker, redundant providers, idempotency keys, bounded queues) to scenarios with costs; compares patterns (e.g. queue-based async workers vs synchronous request/response) in an option/helped/hurt/cost/reversibility table with a rejected alternative; gives module layout with ports per provider, composition root, error and concurrency model and data ownership; writes ADRs with an 'Enforced by' field; produces a minimal compilable TypeScript skeleton with one vertical slice and fakes; adds dependency-cruiser or eslint-plugin-boundaries rules plus a cycle check and one QA-specific check; lists 'deliberately not doing'.

evals.prompt: Write an ADR for our decision to replace the shared Postgres database between the orders and inventory services with an event-driven integration.
evals.expected_output: Uses templates/adr.md; checks the repo for existing ADR location and numbering (else docs/adr/NNNN-title.md); context names the driving scenarios (modifiability/deployability independence, availability) with measures; lists options considered including at least one rejected alternative (e.g. keep shared DB with schema ownership, synchronous API); states decision, consequences (eventual consistency, outbox/dual-write risk, operational cost), sensitivity and tradeoff points; mandatory 'Enforced by' filled with a concrete mechanism (e.g. no cross-service schema access check, contract tests), and 'Revisit when'. No AI attribution.

evals.prompt: Recover the architecture of this repo. I inherited it last week and nobody documented anything.
evals.expected_output: Reads build files, entry points and package tree; runs read-only graph tooling or falls back to grep/build graph and says so; identifies build units, composition root, module dependency graph, cycles, external systems, data stores and deployment units, each with OBSERVED/MEASURED evidence; produces Mermaid sketches of module, C&C and allocation views; states an INFERRED intended model because no docs exist; lists hotspots from git history as pointers, not verdicts; separates AS-IS from any TO-BE suggestions; offers a quick vs deep pass.

evals.prompt: Add architecture tests to our Kotlin Multiplatform project (modules :shared:domain, :shared:data, :androidApp, :iosApp). The domain must never depend on data or on platform code.
evals.expected_output: Starts from the enforcement ladder: first uses Gradle module boundaries (domain module has no dependency on data; implementation vs api), then adds Konsist (or ArchUnit for JVM-only code) tests for rules the build cannot express (no android.*/platform imports in domain, naming of use cases); baselines existing violations and ratchets; names tests after the rule/ADR; wires into the existing test/CI command; flags version-dependent syntax; does not modify build files beyond what the task requires without asking; runs the tests.

evals.prompt: Should orders and billing talk event-driven (Kafka) or request/response (REST)? We have 3 engineers and ~50 orders/minute.
evals.expected_output: Answers in the decision format: one-line recommendation (likely request/response or a simple outbox + queue given team size and load, justified); driving scenarios with measures; tactics; pattern plus runner-up; tradeoffs as sensitivity/tradeoff points (coupling vs consistency vs operational cost); what would change the answer (e.g. more consumers, independent release cadence, 100x load); smallest next step in code. Weighs team size and operational burden; does not recommend Kafka by default.

evals.prompt: Why is this Django monolith so hard to change? Every feature touches five apps. Is it ready to scale to 10x users?
evals.expected_output: Runs the repository review: recovers as-is structure; establishes or asks for top 3 QAs; reflexion comparison; measures hotspots (churn x size) and change coupling across app boundaries, optionally import-linter/pydeps graph; walks the smell catalogue (cyclic app dependencies, god models, fat signals, shared utils); utility tree with 5-8 leaves and analysis of top 3 scenarios with risks, non-risks, sensitivity and tradeoff points; groups into risk themes; now/next/later roadmap where each item has an ADR and a fitness function (e.g. import-linter contracts); rejects a big-bang rewrite unless justified; findings have file:line evidence.

evals.prompt: Document the architecture of this Go service for new team members, using C4 and arc42.
evals.expected_output: Asks or states audience and purpose (descriptive); follows 42010 stakeholders/concerns/viewpoints/views; produces a lean arc42 skeleton with C4 levels 1-3 in Mermaid or Structurizr DSL generated from the recovered graph (go list); includes a view map, ranked quality goals with a conflict rule, intended vs actual layering, ADRs split into embodied vs proposed; links stated rules to enforcing checks (e.g. internal/ packages, go-arch-lint); every AS-IS claim cited.

evals.prompt: We have a cyclic dependency between the 'billing' and 'accounts' packages in our Java app. How do we break it without a big refactor?
evals.expected_output: Cites the cycle with OBSERVED file:line imports in both directions; proposes the smallest structural change (dependency inversion via an interface owned by one side, extracting a shared kernel, or events) with tradeoffs and a runner-up; shows code for the change labelled with file paths; adds a cycle check (ArchUnit slices().should().beFreeOfCycles() or jdeps-based check) wired into the build, flagging version-dependent API; migration steps that keep main green.

evals.prompt: Add a 'favorites' feature to this Android app (feature modules, Hilt, Room). Just get it done properly.
evals.expected_output: Scales the workflow for a small feature: recon of existing module layout and conventions; 1-2 inline scenarios; places the feature in a new or existing feature module following repo idioms; defines repository interface in domain and Room implementation in data; wires via existing Hilt modules; implements one vertical slice with a fake for tests; adds one architecture test or Gradle boundary; at most one ADR; does not introduce new frameworks; build and tests run.

evals.prompt: Can you check this function for off-by-one errors and fix the naming?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is line-level bug hunting and style, outside the skill's scope; says so briefly and hands off to normal code review (or just does ordinary review) without applying the architecture apparatus (no scenarios, ADRs or utility tree).

evals.prompt: Our Python FastAPI service must stay under p95 200 ms while calling two downstream APIs. Review the architecture of the request path and tell me what's missing.
evals.expected_output: Writes the performance and availability scenarios with the stated measure; traces the request path through code with file:line evidence; checks for missing tactics (timeouts, concurrency of the two calls via asyncio.gather, caching, bounded retries, circuit breaker, connection pooling, blocking calls in async handlers); identifies sensitivity and tradeoff points (e.g. cache TTL affects latency and freshness); ranked findings with severity, confidence, fix code, effort and a preventing fitness function (e.g. latency budget test, import-linter rule keeping HTTP clients in adapters); distinguishes MEASURED from INFERRED claims and suggests a load test if no measurements exist.
